response: Very high serum CA 19-9 levels are not a contraindication to pancreaticoduodenectomy. According to research, patients who normalize their CA 19-9 levels after surgery have equivalent survival rates to those with normal preoperative CA 19-9 levels. Therefore, preoperative serum CA 19-9 levels should not be the sole factor in deciding against surgery, as long as careful preoperative staging has been conducted. This suggests that pancreaticoduodenectomy can still be a viable treatment option for patients with very high serum CA 19-9 levels, provided that other factors are taken into consideration.
